nodes.title: scripts/migrate.mjs targets the TEST branch by default (server/db.js dbUrl with TAXILA_DB=test: CONDUCTOR_TEST_DATABASE_URL, else TEST_DATABASE_URL, never a fallback to production); production only with --prod on the command line (TAXILA_DB=prod alone and --prod with TAXILA_DB=test are refused), plus --backup NAME (a Neon backup branch of the target's branch first) or --no-backup on the record. Each migration FILE runs in ONE transaction together with its schema_migrations row (Neon HTTP transaction, or pg begin/commit when DB_DRIVER=pg or the host is not Neon), so a failure leaves the file unapplied and unrecorded; statements are split with string / quoted-name / $tag$ / comment awareness (scripts/migrate-core.mjs splitSql, identical output to the old splitter on all 30 shipped files). --dry-run lists what is pending and writes nothing. --job applies inside the ACA VNet through scripts/region/db-copy.mjs --apply-migrations (psql -1 per file + its row; the sha's migrations ride as a git-archive env var). Reverse if a migration needs a non-transactional statement (create index concurrently): then that file gets an explicit opt-out marker, not a return to statement-by-statement.

Migrate tooling on a throwaway local PostgreSQL 16 (TLS on, verify-full with a self-signed CA; no Neon, no Azure): migrate.mjs (pg driver) --dry-run 30 pending, apply 30 applied, rerun 0 applied; db-copy.sh MODE=apply 30 applied each in one psql -1 transaction, rerun 0, missingMigrations empty; a planted 999_bad.sql (create table, then 1/0) failed at 'apply 999_bad.sql (rolled back)' with the table absent and no schema_migrations row. Refusals exit 2 with one line: TAXILA_DB=prod without --prod, --prod with TAXILA_DB=test, --prod without --backup/--no-backup. Unit tests: tests/migrate-tooling.test.mjs (10, no DB). Not yet run live: --dry-run on the stream's Neon branch (HTTP transaction path), the Neon backup-branch API, the ACA job apply (MIGRATIONS_TGZ ~35 KB as a container env var).

Production releases go through scripts/release.mjs <commit>. The steps are: gate evidence (CI build + every shard, or a clean local stamp); the X37 freeze; capture what is live (web revision + env names, worker image); ACR builds taxila-web:<sha7> and taxila-worker:<sha7> from GitHub AT the commit; migrate.mjs --prod --sha with a Neon backup branch; deploy-azure --image-tag (canary + smoke); a cohort check that every env name the previous web revision carried is still on the new one; deploy-worker --image-tag --jobs, so the worker and both Conductor jobs run the web's commit; a context entry. Progress is saved per commit, and a re-run resumes at the first unfinished step. --rollback moves the web to `previous` and the worker + jobs to the captured image together. ARM calls retry transient failures (network, 408/429/5xx) for idempotent methods only, never a POST that starts something. Reverse if ACR's git context cannot build at a commit sha (then build from a clean worktree upload).

One price book (server/cost/prices.js, MODEL-STACK meter ids, estimates flagged) prices every meter: chat tokens, TTS chars, STT hours, Voice Live minutes, images. Every spend event carries its own usd: model.call, speech.tts (azure.js tts() records it), and stt.session / d5.session / image.call via server/cost/meter.js. A lesson's events (sid = lesson id) roll up into lesson.cost jsonb (migration 040) by meter and lane. scripts/cost.mjs reads by lesson, day or child and reconciles with Cost Management. The bill, not the book, is the truth: change a price only with its meter id. Until the five call sites in docs/patches/from-platform/001 land, lesson.cost covers chat + azure.js TTS only.

taxila-web drains on SIGTERM (server/shutdown.js). It stops accepting new connections, readiness answers 503 'draining', open WebSockets get d5.closed {reason: server_restart} then close 1012 so the D5 client reconnects, and in-flight requests get 20 s before being cut. The trace writer is flushed with a 5 s deadline, then the process exits 0. deploy-azure sets terminationGracePeriodSeconds 30. Reverse if a lesson turn regularly exceeds 20 s (then raise both together).

The owner ops page is GET /api/ops (HTML) + /api/ops/summary. It shows live lessons, lesson-turn p50/p90, 5xx by route, and $ per lesson-minute and per hour from lesson.cost. It answers only a signed-in guardian whose email or sha256 is in TAXILA_OPS_FOR (env, so the owner's account is keyed without a code change, main 2026-11-04); anyone else gets 404. Counts and timings only, and a lesson shows as an 8-char id prefix.

Gate sharding. One-process npm test in the 4-core container: 1,711 s (3,688 tests). The same 379 suites as one process each, 4 at a time: 578 s wall, 0 failing in isolation (tests/shard-weights.json; kit-budget 442 s is the longest single suite, so it sets the critical path). First CI matrix run (PR #28 @ 1bd8c68f, count-split shards): build + 6 shards all green, ~8 min from start to the aggregate `gates` job, slowest shard unit 2/4 ~7 min; the old single job took 17-24 min.

migrate.mjs on the stream's own Neon branch (host sha256 f47b22100116a310) over Neon's HTTP transaction API: --dry-run listed 040 pending (1 statement), the apply ran it in one transaction, and a rerun applied 0. That is the live check of the Neon path that was outstanding in ms-r7-migrate-tooling-local-2026-11-04.
